title: Sensor
description: Definition of a harness sensor (feedback control). A sensor observes the system AFTER the agent acts and produces a Signal optimized for self-correction. Every runtime invocation of a sensor matching this schema MUST emit an output that conforms to schemas/signal.json — referenced here as #/$defs/Signal so tooling can resolve the output contract via chained $ref. References: Boeckeler, 'Harness Engineering' (martinfowler.com); Lopopolo, 'Harness engineering: leveraging Codex…' (openai.com, 2026-02-11).

timeout_ms.description: Hard cap; falls back to cost.latency.timeout_ms when omitted.

exit_code_map.description: Override only when tooling uses non-standard codes (e.g. 2 = 'already exists', treat as pass). When omitted, runner applies the default [{0:pass/info},{*:fail/high}].

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug. Used verbatim as Signal.sensor_id.

version.description: SemVer of the sensor definition. Bump on contract changes.

description.description: One sentence: trigger condition + what is observed + regulation dimension.

kind.description: Sensor category. observation = observes behavior with no fixed expectation (run-project, fetch-logs, fetch-metrics, trace-request, watch-build); verdict describes the health of the observation. assertion = checks against an expectation (unit-test, integration-test, e2e-test, lint, type-check, build, schema-validate); verdict pass/fail is semantic. setup = idempotent auxiliary sensor that makes a precondition true (start-postgres, setup-env-from-example, install-deps-pnpm, login-gcloud); typically referenced via depends_on. Metadata only — the runner treats all three identically; tooling (detect-sensors, listings) uses it to classify and name.

type.description: Execution nature. computational = deterministic, CPU-bound, fast, cheap (linters, type checkers, structural tests, fixed-threshold log/metric queries). inferential = probabilistic, GPU/NPU-bound, slow, expensive (LLM-as-judge, semantic-duplicate detection, AI code review, anomaly classification).

regulation.description: Which dimension of the codebase this sensor regulates (Boeckeler/Fowler taxonomy).

phase.description: Lifecycle stage at which the sensor is invoked.

determinism.description: high = bit-identical reruns; medium = stable across reruns within tolerance; low = inferential without seed.

output.description: How many Signals one invocation emits. single = exactly one Signal carrying the final verdict (the runner ignores subprocess stdout/stderr lines beyond exit code). stream = one Signal per matched output line plus one final aggregate Signal (JSONL on stdout). single forbids execution.output_parsing; stream requires it.

class.description: cheap → safe to run on every change; expensive → gate behind upstream PASS or schedule.

timeout_ms.description: Hard cap. Sensor MUST abort and emit verdict=error past this.

tokens.description: Required when sensor.type = inferential. MUST be omitted when sensor.type = computational.

compute.description: Required when sensor.type = computational. MUST be omitted when sensor.type = inferential.

guardrails.description: What the harness does when cost budgets are exceeded.

fallback_sensor.description: id of a cheaper sensor to delegate to. null disables downgrade.

depends_on.description: IDs of sensors that must run (and PASS) before this one. The runner resolves the transitive closure in topological order and propagates failures. Use to chain setup sensors (start-postgres) or assertion sensors (unit-tests before e2e-tests). Cycles (including self-loops A → A) are detected and abort with exit 1.

requires.description: Preconditions for this sensor. v2 shape: array of discriminated-union items keyed by `kind`. v1 shape (object with tools/permissions/context/env) is still accepted for the duration of this PR; commit 5 drops it.

tools.description: Binaries, MCP servers, CLIs the sensor invokes.

context.description: Repo paths the sensor reads (docs, configs, fixtures).

env.description: Environment variables the runner forwards from its own environment (os.Environ) into the sensor's subprocess. Use this for secrets, project ids, auth tokens, region/profile selectors — anything that would be wrong to hardcode in the sensor JSON. The runner forwards every listed name whose value is set; if a non-optional name is unset at run time it aborts and emits verdict=error with a remediation pointing at the missing var. Declared env vars document intent — the existence of the sensor never depends on the variable being set right now.

description.description: What the variable is and how to obtain it (e.g., 'GitHub PAT with repo:read scope', 'GCP project id for log queries').

optional.description: When true, the runner forwards the value if set but does not abort if missing — useful for env vars that change behaviour rather than being mandatory.

execution.description: Discriminated by sensor.type via the top-level allOf/if-then-else. Computational fields and inferential fields are mutually exclusive.

command.description: Required for both sensor types. Shell invocation (passed to sh -c by the runner) — pipes, redirects, globs and quoted args all work. Should be hermetic and idempotent.

env.description: Environment variables set during subprocess execution. Inferential runner additionally injects HARNESS_PROMPT with the rendered user_prompt_template.

blocking.description: When true, the sensor does not terminate on its own and must be invoked via /start-sensor / /stop-sensor. Forbids cost.latency.timeout_ms; allows execution.graceful_timeout_ms. Other sensors may declare a blocking sensor in depends_on; the orchestrator will start (or attach to) the blocking dep before the dependent runs and stop it at teardown when no other dependent holds it.

graceful_timeout_ms.description: Time to wait between SIGTERM and SIGKILL on /stop-sensor. Applies only when execution.blocking is true. Minimum 100ms to ensure the process has a real chance to react to SIGTERM.

prepare.description: Silent shell commands run before execution.command. Used to satisfy the sensor's preconditions (generate files, populate local .env from .env.example, intermediate builds). NOT observed via patterns; per-step verdict is folded into the sensor's aggregate metadata.lifecycle.prepare. Fail-fast: first non-pass step aborts prepare and skips the main command; teardown still runs.

teardown.description: Silent shell commands run AFTER execution.command with finally semantics — they run on prepare failure, command failure, and command timeout. Per-step results are folded into metadata.lifecycle.teardown; teardown failures contribute warn evidence but do NOT downgrade the aggregate verdict.

exit_code_map.description: Maps process exit codes to verdict/severity. Required for computational sensors; optional for inferential (when omitted, the inferential runner defaults to exit 0 → pass/info, anything else → error/high). Use exit_code='*' as wildcard fallback.

output_parsing.description: Structured rules for turning subprocess output lines into individual Signals. Applies to both computational and inferential sensors. Optional — when absent, only the aggregate Signal is emitted.

patterns.description: Ordered match rules. First pattern that matches a line wins.

captures.description: Map a Signal.evidence field to a 1-based capture-group index in regex.

system_prompt.description: Inferential only. Role-defining system message, no example contamination.

user_prompt_template.description: Inferential only. Template with {{slots}}; demands a single JSON object conforming to the Signal schema.

seed.description: Set when reproducibility matters and the model supports it.

self_correction.description: How the harness consumes this sensor's Signal.

escalation.description: Free-form criteria for human escalation (e.g. 'confidence < 0.6 OR 3 consecutive fails without verdict change').

verification.description: Sensors are code; they need their own harness. Each sensor MUST declare at least one golden case.

fixture.description: Path to fixture or fixture id.

self_test_command.description: Command that runs all fixtures and validates each emitted Signal against signal.json.

blind_spots.description: Explicit limits — bug classes, inputs that produce unstable verdicts, sensor interactions that mask issues. Required honesty for inferential sensors.

calibration.description: REQUIRED when sensor.type=inferential. Captures the confidence threshold and drift policy.

confidence_threshold.description: Below this threshold, the harness MUST downgrade fail → warn.

drift_check_cadence.description: Cron expression or human-readable cadence for re-running golden fixtures.

calibration_set.description: Path or URI to labelled fixtures used to choose the threshold.

references.description: Source articles, ADRs, design docs justifying this sensor.
